name: Firehouse Museum Mamey

location.address: Key West Firehouse Museum, 1026 Grinnell St (corner of Virginia St), Key West, FL 33040

official_register.name: Florida Champion Tree Program (Florida Forest Service)

access: Museum is free (suggested donation $5), open Wednesday to Saturday 10:00 to 14:00, last admission 13:30 (museum's own site, fetched). Register: tree is on City of Key West land between the fire station museum and the building next door. NOT CONFIRMED whether the tree is visible from the Grinnell or Virginia Street sidewalk; no fetched source says.
transport: Old Town Key West, corner of Grinnell and Virginia streets; walkable from the Old Town streets (no transit stop verified by a fetched page, writer must not invent one)
story:
Florida's largest mammee apple tree ends up, every year, as ice cream. The Key West Firehouse Museum holds an annual mamey ice cream social, made with fruit from the tree in its yard, and in June 2024 the tree was still bearing.

It is the state champion of its species on the Florida Forest Service register. In 2018 the county forester measured it at 328 centimetres round at chest height and 14.9 metres tall, with a crown about 17 by 12 metres. He also wrote down its condition: fair, mature and declining. The 2024 fruit is the most recent word on its health.

Nobody recorded when it went in. Firehouse No. 3 was built in 1908, and the museum's account is that the tree followed a few years later. Volunteers threw it a 105th birthday party in 2019, a date worked back from the roughly 21 years a mamey needs before it fruits; a 2024 newspaper caption made it 115. Both are the museum's guess, so call it somewhere between 100 and 120.

One naming trap: "mamey" is also the common name of Pouteria sapota, a different species altogether. The register is specific that this one is Mammea americana.

The tree stands on city land between the museum and the building next door. The museum is free, with a suggested donation, and opens Wednesday to Saturday from 10:00 to 14:00. Whether you can see the crown from the street without going in, we have not been able to confirm.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the state champion mamey in the museum's yard. It stands between the Key West Firehouse Museum and the building next door, at the corner of Grinnell and Virginia streets.

Champion status is about size, not age; no age or girth in the brochure or floridahikes. Alive: park open and tended in the 2022 brochure; lifecheck RECENT (iNaturalist 2026-09-29 near the park) but not tied to this tree; Irma 2017 defoliated the hammock (Commons photos). Flagged: no dated tree-specific confirmation, pin is stop-level. Setting is the point: 7.8-acre remnant of the Brickell Hammock. Willow Bustic champion (OBJECTID 82, 54 in, 57 ft, 2009) is in the same park, see leads. Photo: none in reach (no CC file tied to the champion).

verified_sources: https://vizcaya.org/gardenmound-label/ (Vizcaya's label, fetched 2026-10-18: '200-year old, windswept Live Oak trees'; a video caption on the same page says '100-year-old oak trees')

access: Paid admission to Vizcaya Museum and Gardens; open Wednesday to Monday, closed Tuesday (earlier pass, hours not refetched). Mound is a short walk up stone steps from the formal gardens.
transport: Vizcaya Metrorail station, about 500 m (5 to 10 minute walk) from the entrance.
verify_notes: Ensemble: four oaks on one artificial hill (built 1914 to 1922 for James Deering), one place to stand. Age conflict recorded: Vizcaya's own label says 200 years, a caption on the same page says 100; sofiascountrygardens says large when moved about a century ago. No source gives a girth. Range 100 to 220 is institutional PR, not a measurement; page should state it. Alive: Vizcaya's own page describes current storm-resilience trimming of these oaks and a 2025 dated item on the same site; no tree-dated photo seen. Pin is the property centroid (register points for Vizcaya champions sit at 25.7433 to 25.7456, -80.2132 to -80.2107); mound coordinate not found (Nominatim empty). The 'small site' radius is a stretch (mound plus steps); drop location_site if the writer finds it too broad. Paid entry.

Vizcaya itself names a Red Stopper champion, which is the owner-of-ground corroboration, but its caption does not say which of the several Vizcaya redberry stopper records (PK 10, 877, 895, 1023) it shows; 1023 is the only one currently titled National Champion, the others pending or emeritus. Slender hammock tree, remarkable as the largest of its species in the US, not for age. Weak page: no photo, no age.

verify_notes: Register: circumference 60 in (152 cm), height 74 ft (22.6 m), crown 25 by 21 ft, measured Apr 2012, titled Florida Challenger, matching Vizcaya's wording. Not independently proven to be the same palm (Vizcaya gives no location), but only one Vizcaya royal palm record exists. Age: Vizcaya documents the Cuban palms arriving around 1916 to 1921 (dated delivery photo 1921) and says one remains; a palm of that planting is roughly a century, but the page does not state this specimen's year, so treat the range as derived from 'one remaining' original, not a measured age. Palm girth is a trunk circumference, not a tree-ring measure. Alive: Vizcaya's page (2025 items) still says it remains; register 2012; not tree-dated. Pin is the register coordinate, approximate.
